bell-state-preparation.paperTitle: Transformation of quantum states using uniformly controlled rotations
bell-state-preparation.authors: Mikko Möttönen, Juha J. Vartiainen, Ville Bergholm, Martti M. Salomaa
bell-state-preparation.anchorLabel: Möttönen et al. Eq. (1) + Sec. III
bell-state-preparation.sourceMeaning: Eq. (1) fixes the general n-qubit state-vector convention, while Sec. III states the state-preparation problem as finding U with U|a> = |b>.
bell-state-preparation.caseRelation: ASPBE specializes that general contract to the Bell target (|00>+|11>)/sqrt(2). The H-then-CX witness is a textbook teaching circuit; we do not claim that this two-gate Bell example is copied from Möttönen et al.

mottonen-dense-state-preparation.paperTitle: Transformation of quantum states using uniformly controlled rotations
mottonen-dense-state-preparation.authors: Mikko Möttönen, Juha J. Vartiainen, Ville Bergholm, Martti M. Salomaa
mottonen-dense-state-preparation.sourceMeaning: Eq. (6) shows one uniformly controlled y-rotation eliminating one qubit, Eq. (7) composes the recursive preparation route, Eq. (8) gives the rotation angles, and Fig. 3 displays the resulting state-preparation circuit.
mottonen-dense-state-preparation.caseRelation: ASPBE instantiates this UCRY architecture on one exact two-qubit dense real-amplitude target. The finite target/unitary proof is certified; the paper-wide arbitrary-n gate-count theorem is not claimed reproduced.

grover-rudolph-product-state-preparation.paperTitle: Creating superpositions that correspond to efficiently integrable probability distributions
grover-rudolph-product-state-preparation.sourceMeaning: Eq. (1) is the target probability-amplitude state, Eq. (3) is the recursive one-qubit refinement, and Eq. (6) realizes that refinement by a controlled rotation after coherently computing the split angle.
grover-rudolph-product-state-preparation.caseRelation: ASPBE chooses a two-bit product distribution as an exact finite specialization. The factorized two-rotation winner is an ASPBE same-target optimization; it is not stated as a resource theorem in the source paper.

sparse-three-state-preparation.paperTitle: Nearly Optimal Circuit Size for Sparse Quantum State Preparation
sparse-three-state-preparation.sourceMeaning: Eq. (1) represents a d-sparse state by its nonzero amplitudes and basis labels. Eq. (2) is the exact unitary preparation contract, including clean ancillary qubits.
sparse-three-state-preparation.caseRelation: ASPBE sets n=3 and d=3 and proves one exact finite witness of Eq. (2). The 5-vs-15 zero-branch pruning comparison is a finite ASPBE benchmark and is not presented as a reproduction of the paper's asymptotic Theorem 1.

robin-ghl-one-term.sourceKind: paper reproduction plus certified fixed-benchmark improvement
robin-ghl-one-term.paperTitle: Quantum Framework for Simulating Linear PDEs with Robin Boundary Conditions
robin-ghl-one-term.authors: Nikita Guseynov, Xiajie Huang, Nana Liu
robin-ghl-one-term.sourceMeaning: Eq. (9) defines the Robin finite-difference operator used by the N=8 benchmark; Theorem 3 supplies sparse Hamiltonian access; Theorem 4 turns that access into a block encoding; Fig. 4 gives the source circuit route used for fixed-instance reconstruction.
robin-ghl-one-term.caseRelation: ASPBE reconstructs the fixed source route, proves exact clean-block semantics, and then certifies a same-target lexicographically better fixed-N circuit. Query-level improvement beyond the paper theorem is not claimed.
